test_title: PYST 05: SSC Stenographer - English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 11 Dec 2024 - Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Calling me a friend, Surjit Singh encouraged me and advised me not to lose heart.

options.text: Surjit Singh demanded, “Cheer up, friend. Do not lose heart.”
Surjit Singh ordered me, “Cheer up, friend. Do not lose heart.”
Surjit Singh asked me, “Cheer up, friend. Do not lose heart.”
Surjit Singh said, “Cheer up, friend. Do not lose heart.”

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** Calling me a friend, Surjit Singh encouraged me and advised me not to lose heart.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"encouraged me and advised me" becomes "Cheer up, friend. Do not lose heart."**
 
 
• Indirect suggestion "encouraged me and advised me" is converted to direct advice "Cheer up, friend. Do not lose heart."
 
• The pronoun "me" is understood and omitted in direct speech.
 
 
 
• **"Calling me a friend" remains "friend"**
 
 
• Directly addressing as "friend" retains the informal and encouraging tone.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: "encouraged me and advised me"
 
• Converted to: "said," which is a neutral reporting verb suitable for friendly advice.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "Cheer" and ends with a period ".".
 
• Reporting clause follows the quoted speech, starting with a lowercase letter after the comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"“Cheer up, friend. Do not lose heart.” said Surjit Singh."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Surjit Singh demanded, “Cheer up, friend. Do not lose heart.”" 

 
 
• The verb "demanded" suggests a forceful tone, which is inappropriate for friendly encouragement.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "Surjit Singh ordered me, “Cheer up, friend. Do not lose heart.”" 
 
 
• The verb "ordered" implies a command rather than a friendly piece of advice.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Surjit Singh asked me, “Cheer up, friend. Do not lose heart.”" 
 
 
• The verb "asked" is not suitable as it typically introduces questions, not advice or encouragement.
